meta.about: Data of Learn research studio R7 (r07-cost-carbon-properly), Cost and carbon done properly. The study, its authors, its consultancy, its city and its transit agency are fictional, and every fleet, price and cost input is illustrative, in 2025 dollars. Two numbers are real and dated: diesel's CO2 per gallon (EIA) and the U.S. grid's average CO2 per kWh in 2023 (EIA). The lesson's script recomputes every number the page shows from these inputs, and its test checks each one.

study.title: Electric buses for Port Alder: cheaper and carbon-free
study.authors: R. Okonjo and L. Varga, Harbourline Consulting (fictional), report to Port Alder Transit (fictional), 2026
study.headline: Replacing Port Alder Transit's 40 oldest diesel buses with battery-electric buses saves {saving} a year and cuts the fleet's CO₂ by {cutPct}.
study.method: Annual costs over a 12-year bus life at a 3% real discount rate; CO₂ from the buses' tailpipes.

plan.text: The {buses} buses bought in {oldYear} retire in 2026; {buses} new diesel buses replace them ({newMpg} mpg, {newMaint} a mile in repairs) unless the board funds another option.

electric.meter: at the depot meter, charging losses included

fixes.label: A fair baseline
fixes.short: new diesel buses as the counterfactual

fixes.label: Grid costs
fixes.short: depot connection and demand charges added

fixes.label: The credit once
fixes.short: the second count of the credit removed

boundaryItems.label: Bus purchases
boundaryItems.fb: in the cost only, for both fleets; making the buses is outside both CO₂ counts, a limit that a life-cycle study would add (A11).

boundaryItems.label: Electricity for charging
boundaryItems.fb: the study pays for charging but counts none of its CO₂. On one boundary each fleet's energy counts where it is burned, at the tailpipe or the power plant.

boundaryItems.label: Diesel fuel
boundaryItems.fb: it is inside both: its price in the cost, its CO₂ at the tailpipe.

boundaryItems.label: Repairs
boundaryItems.fb: in the cost only, for both fleets alike; their CO₂ is small and outside both counts.

counterfactuals.label: Keep the 2009 buses running 12 more years
counterfactuals.fb: the agency's replacement plan retires them in 2026, and the study already prices new buses, then runs them like the old ones.

counterfactuals.label: Buy 40 new diesel buses, as the replacement plan says
counterfactuals.fb: that is what would happen without the project. New buses burn less fuel and need fewer repairs.

counterfactuals.label: Buy 40 diesel-electric hybrids
counterfactuals.fb: a real option worth comparing, but not what happens without the project: the plan names diesel buses.

creditLines.label: In the capital line: buses net of the credit
creditLines.fb: that count is the right one: it takes the credit off the price when it is paid, up front. Remove the other.

creditLines.label: In the benefits: the credit again, as {creditYear} a year
creditLines.fb: the same {credit}, counted a second time as yearly income. Count it once.

creditLines.label: Neither: the agency gains it, and so does the state
creditLines.fb: the state pays it, so for the two together it moves money and saves nothing. Count it once, in the agency's ledger.

exemplars.title: Two audit notes on the same study
exemplars.task: Audit the Port Alder study and say what its conclusion becomes.
exemplars.note: Both notes are illustrative, on the course's fictional study.

parts.note: No flaw is named, so no one can check or fix it.

parts.text: Electric buses still have no emissions
parts.note: True at the tailpipe only; the power plants that charge them emit.
No number, no baseline, no 'whose cost'.
It says nothing a reader could act on.

parts.text: charging is in the cost but its CO₂ is not; at EIA's 2023 U.S. average factor, the electric fleet is attributed {eCO2} a year.
parts.note: Names the mismatch, the fix and the factor's source.

parts.text: without the project the agency buys new diesel buses ({newMpg} mpg), not the 2009 fleet ({oldMpg} mpg).
parts.note: The counterfactual, stated from the agency's own plan.

parts.text: add the depot connection ({depot} up front) and demand charges ({demand} a year).
parts.note: Up front and annual kept apart.

parts.text: counted once, in the capital line; the second {creditYear} a year removed.
parts.note: Says which count stays and why.

parts.text: the prices, miles and {kWhPerMile} kWh per mile are the study's illustrative assumptions; the replacement plan is the agency's own document (fictional); the CO₂ factors are EIA's published figures.
parts.note: Each key input's evidence status, as the Realism bar asks.

parts.text: making the buses and batteries, street air and noise, grid losses, a grid that gets cleaner, battery replacement.
parts.note: What the audit does not count, said.

parts.text: for the agency, electric costs {extra} a year more and lowers attributed CO₂ by {cut} ({cutPctA}), about {perTonne} per tonne, if the grid is at the 2023 U.S. average.
parts.note: Cost and attributed CO₂ on one boundary, whose cost, and the condition that moves it most.

diff.label: Numbers
diff.good: Cost, CO₂ and cost per tonne

diff.label: Whose cost
diff.good: The agency's, with the credit once

diff.label: Evidence and limits
diff.good: Each input's status; what is left out

ladder.title: How far up the ladder is each number?
ladder.lede: A saving is only as sure as its inputs. Place each statement about Port Alder's buses on the evidence ladder.

rungs.label: Operating
rungs.text: It runs and is counted as in service.

rungs.label: At design output
rungs.text: It delivers what it was built to deliver.

off.label: Not on the ladder: a projection

items.text: The transit board voted the money for 40 electric buses.
items.note: Funded: money committed, nothing built yet.

items.text: Every permit the depot's new service connection needs has been issued.
items.note: Permitted: the authorities have said yes, but nothing is built yet; its cost estimate is still an estimate.

items.text: Ten electric buses have carried passengers since March.
items.note: Operating: in service, but a few months do not show a year's energy use.

items.text: For a full year, winter included, the ten buses ran their planned routes within their energy target.
items.note: At design output: planned service at a measured 2.2 kWh per mile.

items.text: The audit's cost per attributed tonne of CO₂.
items.note: A projection: a model's output from inputs on several rungs, not a stage of anything built.

rubric.title: Rate your audit note against the rubric
rubric.lede: The course rubric's own words, for the two competences R7 builds.

competences.look: cost and CO₂ for the same service, alternatives and years, the emissions question named (an attributed share or a change in the system), and whose cost each number is.
each key input with its evidence status, and a list of what the audit leaves out.

checklist.label: Same service
checklist.text: Both options deliver the same service: the same routes and miles, the same years.

checklist.label: One boundary
checklist.text: Cost and CO₂ cover the same service, alternatives and years; whose costs count and which emissions stages are in are stated, with what is left out.

checklist.label: A stated counterfactual
checklist.text: One sentence says what happens without the project, from a plan or a rule, not a convenient past.

checklist.label: The emissions question
checklist.text: [[average-emission-factor|Average]] or [[marginal-emission-factor|marginal]] factor, and why: whose share of the grid's CO₂, or what a change in demand changes.

checklist.label: Grid and connection costs
checklist.text: Upgrades, demand charges and connection fees are priced, with who pays them.

checklist.label: Credits once
checklist.text: Each grant or credit appears in one line, and is a transfer for the state and the agency together.

checklist.label: Up front and annual apart
checklist.text: One-time amounts and their annual equivalents are labeled, with the rate and the life.

checklist.label: The condition that moves it
checklist.text: The input that changes the conclusion most is named, with the result at its other values.

grid.label: EIA, Frequently Asked Questions: How much carbon dioxide is produced per kilowatthour of U.S. electricity generation?

losses.label: EIA, Frequently Asked Questions: How much electricity is lost in electricity transmission and distribution in the United States?

units: Units: t is a metric tonne (1,000 kg); mpg is miles per U.S. gallon; a demand charge is dollars per kW of the month's highest draw (a kW-month), billed each month.
